canonical_digit_convention.digit_index: LSD-first: index i is the coefficient of 3^i
canonical_digit_convention.alignment: LSD-align encode(x) with encode(W(x)); pad the shorter word with 0 on the MSD side, matching addition
canonical_digit_convention.self_reverse: when bt_length(x)=bt_length(W(x)), s_i = d_i + d_{L-1-i} on the canonical word of x
canonical_digit_convention.leading_zeros: encode strips canonical leading zeros before pairing
canonical_digit_convention.negatives: encode is sign-aware; digits lie in {-1,0,+1}
canonical_digit_convention.zero: encode(0) is the one-digit word (0); s=(0,)

pair_definition.s_i: left_i + right_i, the raw aligned trit sum before rewrite_sum
pair_definition.not_carry: s_i does not include incoming carry and is not a carry statistic
pair_definition.P0: number of aligned positions with s_i = 0
pair_definition.Pplus: number of aligned positions with s_i > 0
pair_definition.Pminus: number of aligned positions with s_i < 0
pair_definition.R: largest LSD index i with s_i != 0, or -1 if every s_i = 0

candidate_statements.name: cancellation_majority_blocks_growth
candidate_statements.exact_statement: P0(x) > P2(x) implies bt_length(T(x)) - bt_length(x) <= 0 for the one-step addition T(x)=x+W(x)
candidate_statements.motivation: A reverse pairing with more cancelling positions (s_i=0) than constructive collisions (|s_i|=2) should not grow canonical length. K is not fitted: the relation is the direct P0/P2 comparison with ΔL.
candidate_statements.relevant_domain: one-step reverse-plus-add states with P0(x) > P2(x)
candidate_statements.expected_yield: an exact cancellation-versus-construction law for length change
candidate_statements.cheapest_falsifier: the first frozen seed with P0>P2 whose canonical length grows

candidate_statements.name: pair_sign_imbalance_matches_successor_sign
candidate_statements.exact_statement: If P+(x) != P-(x) then sign(T(x)) = sign(P+(x)-P-(x)) for the one-step addition T(x)=x+W(x)
candidate_statements.motivation: Reversal preserves the trit multiset, so any sign of T must come from aligned constructive versus destructive pair sums, not from the digit inventory of x alone.
candidate_statements.relevant_domain: one-step reverse-plus-add states with P+ != P-
candidate_statements.expected_yield: an exact pair-majority rule for sign(T)
candidate_statements.cheapest_falsifier: the first frozen seed whose pair-sign majority disagrees with sign(T)
candidate_statements.failure_mechanism: Pair-sign majority disagrees with sign(T): P+=4, P-=3, sign(T(-672))=-1 for -672->-448. Equal-weight pair counts ignore place value 3^i.

candidate_statements.name: length_growth_requires_top_pair
candidate_statements.exact_statement: bt_length(T(x)) - bt_length(x) >= 1 implies s_{n-1} != 0, where n is the LSD-aligned pair length and s_{n-1} is the highest aligned pair sum
candidate_statements.motivation: If where the interaction occurs matters more than how often, length growth should require a nonzero pair at the MSD-aligned position rather than a count of |s_i|=2 anywhere.
candidate_statements.expected_yield: an exact positional obstruction for length growth
candidate_statements.cheapest_falsifier: the first frozen seed whose length grows while the highest pair is 0
